subject: RE: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — Latency & Throughput A/B test plan + next steps
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Khatri <priya.khatri@globex.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — quick follow-up and initial ask

Hi Marissa — great call today, thanks for walking us through Redwood's architecture. A couple of things from our side:

1) We'd like a repeatable A/B plan comparing Redwood hosted API vs our current hyperscaler-managed endpoint (AWS SageMaker/X endpoint) focusing on p95/p99 latency for 256/1024 token responses and tokens/sec at sustained loads.
2) Can Rafael share the exact test harness you use (concurrency, payloads, model variants, quantization settings)?
3) We also need to see cold-start behavior and tokenization differences that might explain output variance.

Attached is a short CSV with our sample prompt set and current baseline numbers. We'll prioritize this if we can get a short plan and timeline.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, AI Platform
Globex Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
Cc: Priya Khatri <priya.khatri@globex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-30T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — quick follow-up and initial ask

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the prompt set. Rafael & Connor are looped to own the bench plan. High level:

- We'll run an A/B comparing Redwood hosted API (pinned model 1.3, INT8 quant) vs your hyperscaler endpoint (we'll run against the config you provided).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec (steady-state and 60s sustained windows), and cold-start latency.
- Payloads: 256-token and 1k-token responses (we'll include 1024 as requested) — both single-turn prompts and a small multi-turn prompt subset.
- Concurrency plan: ramp to target concurrency in steps: 1, 5, 25, 100, 500, 1k (depending on your capacity). We'll collect 10k inferences per step for stability.

Rafael — can you attach the harness and the initial scripts? Connor — after Rafael shares, can you propose the exact run matrix and expected wall time?

Proposed timeline: bench plan by EOD Monday (3/30), initial runs Wed/Thu, results and p95/p99 summary by Friday. If that works for you Alex, we'll schedule a 30-min sync after the results.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

-- Attachment: redwood_globex_initial_benchmarks_v1.csv (text/csv, 24KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>, Priya Khatri <priya.khatri@globex.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T13:42:00Z
Subject: Redwood — A/B benchmark harness and run matrix (draft)

Hi all — attaching the draft harness and run matrix. Key details:

- Harness: Go-based load generator + Python results aggregator. Uses your prompt CSV; supports variable batch sizes, KV cache warmup, and both streaming and non-streaming modes.
- Model variants: Redwood-hosted model v1.3 (INT8), Redwood-hosted model v1.3 (FP16), hyperscaler endpoint as provided by Globex (baseline).
- Quantization note: INT8 on our runtime gives ~1.6-2.2x tokens/sec depending on sequence length; we'll surface per-token latency.
- Run matrix (per sequence length): concurrency steps [1,5,25,100,500,1000], collect 10k inferences per concurrency point. Record p50/p95/p99, median tokens/sec, 60s rolling tokens/sec, and p99 cold-start after 30m idle.
- Environment: Redwood tests run from our us-east cluster (closest to your infra). If you prefer a region-specific run (eu/apac), tell us.

Open questions for Globex: can you provide the hyperscaler endpoint auth and a brief note on invocation (batching enabled? max batch size?) so we can match configs. Also, do you want streaming responses enabled for either side? Streaming can reduce perceived latency for long outputs and changes tokens/sec accounting.

Connor — I'll need your help to validate our bucket sizes and to add the synthetic jitter to model real client behavior.

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

-- Attachment: redwood_ab_test_plan.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 48KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Khatri <priya.khatri@globex.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-01T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood — A/B benchmark harness and run matrix (draft)

Rafael — thanks for the detailed plan. A few clarifications:

- We'll provide the hyperscaler endpoint auth via a short-lived key and note about batching (our endpoint does server-side batching up to 64 requests; we can disable to match Redwood's batch behavior if needed).
- Streaming: let's test both streaming and non-streaming for the 1k-token responses. Please include measured perceived latency (time-to-first-token) in results.
- Cold-start: we care about p99 cold-starts because some of our traffic is bursty — please ensure you run the 30m idle cold-starts at least 3x per config.

One ask on presentation: can you provide a CSV with raw latency samples as well as a summary? Our infra team likes the raw data for sanity checks.

We'll aim to share the auth by EOD Monday (4/5). Looking forward to the runs.

Best,
Alex
